chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who gave charity to his children who had reached maturity, he said: 'If they do not take possession of it before he dies, then it becomes inheritance. But if he gives charity to those among his children who have not reached maturity, it is permissible, because the parent is the one who manages their affairs.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'One should not take back the charity once it has been given sincerely for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ: sincerely for the sake of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a parent giving charity to minor versus adult children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), distinguishing between gifts to mature children, which remain revocable until possession, and those to minors, which are irrevocable due to the parent's guardianship. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that 'walayah' (guardianship) over a minor's assets allows the parent to finalize the gift, whereas mature children retain independent ownership rights. The Imam further reinforces the spiritual merit of the act by noting that charity given sincerely for Allah's sake should not be reclaimed, aligning with the concept of *hibah* in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5585 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as), that he said regarding a man who gave charity to his children who had reached maturity:
"If they do not take possession of it before his death, then it becomes inheritance. But if he gives charity to his minor children, it is permissible because the parent manages their affairs."
Imam (as) also said: "One should not take back a charity once it has been given sincerely for the sake of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."
